prompt: Peroxide + HBr gives anti-Markovnikov addition to alkenes via a radical chain. But peroxide + HCl does NOT. Why does the chain fail with HCl?

options.label: H-Cl is too strong (~103 kcal/mol) — the step 'R• + HCl → RH + Cl•' is endothermic and can't propagate
Cl• is too small — it rebounds off the alkene without adding, breaking the chain at the first propagation step
Peroxides don't initiate with HCl because the ROOH + HCl acid-base reaction quenches the initiator
HCl is too polar — it adds ionically Markovnikov before any radical chain can get started

explanation: Both propagation steps must be feasible. H-Br BDE (~87 kcal/mol) is low enough that Br• can abstract H from HBr and keep the chain going. H-Cl BDE is ~103 — the needed step is too endothermic. HI has the opposite problem (I• addition is too slow). Only HBr threads the needle — a classic 'why only HBr' result.
